messages:
alex: Heads-up — running into a weird ESM/CJS parity problem when bundling the JS SDK for an edge sample app (vite + rollup). Build succeeds but runtime crashes in the edge worker with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')`

alex: Minimal repro: app uses "type: "module"" and imports the SDK like `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'`. Vite + esbuild produce a bundle, but when running under the edge runtime it chokes.

alex: Paste of package.json deps:
```json
"type": "module",
"dependencies": {
  "@redwood/inference": "0.12.0",
  "whatwg-fetch": "^3.6.0"
}
```

alex: Vite config has `ssr: { noExternal: [] }` and I tried `noExternal: ['@redwood/inference']` which made it worse.

alex: Runtime stack:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')
 at Function.Module._resolveFilename (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:... )
 at eval (sdk-entry.cjs.js:12:45)
```

alex: Also seeing TS complaints: imports of types `import type { Client } from '@redwood/inference'` resolve to something that the compiler thinks is `any` — typings seem dual-published but tooling picks wrong entry.

taylor: annoying. do you have a tiny repo I can clone? :eyes:

alex: yeah i'll spin one up but i wanted to dump the config here first in case someone has seen it.

jamie: two common causes: 1) SDK publishes both cjs and esm and bundlers pick different entries, 2) some packages ship conditional exports that break older rollup/vite resolver logic. did you check package.exports?

alex: exports in node_modules/@redwood/inference/package.json:
```json
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```

riley: that looks correct. but older vite (or esbuild transform) sometimes rewrites dynamic requires and ends up pulling the CJS wrapper into an ESM runtime, which causes the prototype errors. try `optimizeDeps.exclude` or `ssr: { external: ['@redwood/inference'] }` to force runtime to use published files?

alex: tried exclude, didn't help. `ssr.external` also didn't. i added `commonjsOptions: { transformMixedEsModules: true }` which removed the prototype error but then types are wrong at dev time.

samir: quick workaround that worked for another project: alias the import to the explicit ESM build in vite config: `alias: { '@redwood/inference': '/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.js' }`. Not great but useful for a repro/temporary patch.

alex: aliasing to ESM did let the edge worker run, thanks. but we shouldn't have to do that — this is onboarding friction for devs. sample apps currently use naive `import` and break on first run.

jamie: agreed. we should make the SDK provide a single clear main entry for bundlers or add a `module` field that Vite consistently picks. Also the published d.ts should be adjacent to the ESM entry or use `types` conditional export.

taylor: can we add a note to the sample app README about the vite workaround and include a minimal vite.config snippet? saves new devs a wasted hour.

alex: i'll open a PR on sample-apps with the alias + comment. also opening an upstream issue for SDK team — tag: @eng-ml?

riley: please include these repro steps in the issue:
1) `git clone https://.../minimal-edge-vite-repro` (placeholder)
2) `npm i` (with `type: module`)
3) `npm run build && npm run start:edge`
4) observe prototype/read error in edge runtime

alex: created GH issue #1428 with logs and repo link (placeholder). cc @samir @jamie

deploy-bot: New issue created: RED-PLAT/SDK#1428 by alex — "ESM/CJS parity causes edge runtime prototype error with vite"

samir: next technical steps for SDK: 1) confirm package.json exports are resolvable by vite/esbuild, 2) add a `module` map or `exports` fallback that points to esm for bundlers, 3) make types resolvable via top-level `types` field and/or `exports.types`, 4) add test in sample-app CI to build with vite and run smoke in edge runtime.

alex: i'll add sample-app PR and link it to the issue. for now, adding the alias + one-liner in onboarding docs so new hires don't hit this. :thumbsup:

taylor: thanks for triaging quickly. when the SDK team has a patch, can we include a small migration note for teams that pinned older versions?

alex: yup. I'll keep the thread updated with PR numbers.

riley: fyi — also saw a case where `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` vs `import * as Redwood` behaved differently across bundlers. recommend tests for both forms in the sample app matrix.

alex: great call. adding both to the repro matrix.
